purpose: Ground a controlled memory-representation intervention in a public long-term conversation while preserving turn-level provenance.

dataset.name: LoCoMo
dataset.paperTitle: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents

license.name: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International
license.useBoundary: Research and portfolio case study; attribution required; no claim of commercial reuse rights.

dataset.generationBoundary: LoCoMo conversations were generated between LLM agents with assigned personas. They are public research artifacts, not verified records of real users.

selection.caseDomain: Scheduling and low-burden activity planning under changing work-life constraints

cutoff.rule: Only the listed dialogue records at or before D26:20 may support a memory claim. Later turns and annotations may not be consulted while drafting M1, M2, or M3.

selectionRationale: The focal speaker remains the same across every substantive memory claim.
The history contains an enduring value, an isolated high-intensity aspiration, recent work stress, low-burden coping behavior, a temporary pet-related constraint, and a fixed Sunday commitment.
The evidence supports the existing local scheduling task without requiring a real calendar account.
The history contains tensions that a stable profile could flatten, making temporal and uncertainty-aware representation meaningful.

rejectedAlternative.reason: The initially noticed preference shift belonged to John, while the strategy-game development intention belonged to James. Combining them as one user's memory would violate speaker attribution.

claimBoundary: The presence and text of a selected dataset record are observed at the dataset boundary.
Statements about Andrew's preferences, plans, or state are speaker-reported claims inside a generated conversation, not independently verified real-world facts.
A derived memory representation may summarize selected evidence but may not upgrade uncertainty, recurrence, duration, or current applicability without marking the inference.
The case study may describe observable runtime differences after memory exposure but may not identify a hidden model mechanism or claim a general causal memory effect.

dataHandling.rawDatasetPolicy: Keep the downloaded dataset under the gitignored locomodata/ directory.
dataHandling.committedDerivedDataPolicy: Commit only the manifest, evidence ledger, bounded attributed excerpts, representations, synthetic workspace, and privacy-safe traces.
dataHandling.postCutoffPolicy: Do not use post-cutoff dialogue or annotations to create, repair, or evaluate a representation.
dataHandling.attribution: Cite the LoCoMo paper and repository in the case-study README and any public demo.
